g.text: GyanPath — how the learning agent works
You give one topic. It builds a roadmap you approve, then loops every task: find sources → fetch → research → teach → quiz → project → next.
⌨️ A topic — typed into the Next.js screen → POST /api/start
🖱️ A decision — confirm or edit the roadmap, take the quiz, accept the project
🔁 A resume — the same session_id reattaches to the same LangGraph thread
State is checkpointed (InMemorySaver), so the graph can
pause for a user and resume on the next HTTP call.
6–10 tasks, beginner → advanced and strictly about the topic.
The model returns {tasks:[…]}; a two-task fallback keeps the
The graph halts and returns the task list. No lesson is
generated until you approve the plan.
add · delete · edit by index — then straight
Exa docs and YouTube search run in parallel. Dedupe, drop
blocked domains (Medium, Substack…), score preferred docs,
widen the query if fewer than 3 survive, keep the top 5.
Articles: trafilatura → BeautifulSoup → Exa highlights. Videos:
transcript. Anything under 1,000 characters is thrown away.
Synthesise ONLY from the fetched sources — summary, key points,
code, examples, takeaways. Falls back to model knowledge if
Turns the notes into a structured lesson with headings, steps
The lesson goes back to the UI and the graph waits for a yes or

Only the questions are sent to the browser.

SCORE: X/3 — parsed by regex for the UI.
yes → write a brief · no → move on.

LOCAL STATE — in memory only, no database yet
a plain dict; lost on restart, unsafe with
project — progress_node must not clear it
HTTP SURFACE — every call resumes the same graph
POST /challenge — accept project or move on
SCREENS — one page, driven by a phase reducer
FOUR PLACES THE GRAPH STOPS — interrupt() checkpoints
roadmap_review — hands back the task list; accepts add / delete / edit / confirm
quiz_permission — hands back the finished lesson and its resources; waits for yes / no
quiz_answer — hands back the 3 questions only — correct answers stay in state
challenge_prompt — hands back the score and feedback; asks yes / no for a project
Solid arrow — the main path, one step to the next.
Dashed arrow — this step reads state or calls a tool.
Amber card — the graph pauses here for you (interrupt).
GyanPath · LangGraph + FastAPI + Next.js · roadmap, live sources, graded quizzes and project briefs for any topic.
